notes: The verified anthology witness prints the morphologically difficult `வந்தேன் தவழ்ந்தாய்?`. The English keeps the visible subject shift (`I came` / `did you crawl?`) rather than silently emending the Tamil to a familiar or smoother reading.
The dust/flower-garland collision is kept concrete.

english_lines: Will you not look, my rosewater treasure?
We fell with the very roots,
Even the life we lived like a kingdom has fallen,
In this ruined womb of mine you were born, my king!
notes: `சீரோடு வாழ்ந்தோம் / வேரோடு சாய்ந்தோம்` is kept as a compact splendour/roots reversal rather than paraphrased.
`ராஜாங்கம்` remains `kingdom`, and the direct `ராஜா!` address remains `my king!`.
The harsh `பாழான எந்தன் வயிற்றில்` image is not softened.

english_lines: Had you been born in a bird's home,
Food, just to end your hunger,
Would have come flying to you;
Crores upon crores of poor people wither,
You were born, my king, in a land where the grandees live!
notes: The bird/food-flying image is preserved literally enough to keep the bitter comparison between animal care and human poverty.
`கோடானுகோடி` remains `crores upon crores`, retaining the Tamil numerical-social register rather than replacing it with a vague `millions`.
`சீமான்கள்` is rendered as `grandees` to retain the class contrast with `ஏழை மாந்தர்`.

translator_notes: The translation preserves the maternal lament's repeated `Why were you born?` rather than varying it for literary elegance.
The song's movement from fallen household/kingdom imagery to the contrast between poor people and wealthy grandees is retained as a political-social structure, not reduced to private grief alone.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
